summary: Elon Musk built his wealth and institutional power through online payments, Tesla, SpaceX and the companies now grouped around X and xAI. He converted that power into electoral influence by spending at least $277 million for Donald Trump and other Republicans in 2024, serving briefly as a White House adviser associated with DOGE, and becoming the largest known donor of the 2026 midterm cycle. His political reach now combines campaign money, ownership of a major communications platform and companies whose launch, satellite and technology businesses are deeply connected to the federal government.

works.title: The Secret Tesla Motors Master Plan

chapters.title: Pretoria, Canada and Silicon Valley
chapters.dek: An immigrant path through two countries, two degrees and the first internet company.
chapters.body:
Elon Reeve Musk was born in Pretoria, South Africa, on June 28, 1971. He moved to Canada in 1989, drawing citizenship from his Canadian-born mother, and moved to the United States for university. He earned bachelor's degrees in physics and economics at the University of Pennsylvania and briefly entered a Stanford graduate program before leaving to work on an internet business [[biography-2026, cnn-immigration-2024, stanford-bio]].

In 1995 Musk and his brother Kimbal started Zip2, which sold online directory and mapping tools to newspapers. Compaq acquired it in 1999 for $307 million; Time reported that Musk received about $22 million. The sale supplied the capital for his next company and established the pattern that defined his career: reinvesting the proceeds of one technology business into a much more capital-intensive one [[time-fortune-2021, tesla-bio]].

chapters.title: X.com, PayPal and the first large fortune
chapters.dek: A bank, a merger, removal as chief executive and a stake that kept appreciating.
chapters.body:
Musk used part of the Zip2 proceeds to found X.com, an online bank, in 1999. X.com merged with Peter Thiel's Confinity in March 2000. The combined company concentrated on the PayPal payments product; its board removed Musk as chief executive later that year and installed Thiel. Musk remained the largest shareholder [[time-fortune-2021]].

When eBay bought PayPal for $1.5 billion in October 2002, Musk received roughly $180 million. The sale did more than make him wealthy: it funded the two companies that became the main sources of his economic and public power, SpaceX and Tesla [[time-fortune-2021, tesla-bio]].

chapters.title: SpaceX and Tesla
chapters.dek: Private capital, federal contracts and a pair of companies that changed launch and electric-car markets.
chapters.body:
Musk founded SpaceX in May 2002 with the stated goal of reducing launch costs and making human life multiplanetary. After three failed Falcon 1 launches, the fourth reached orbit in 2008; the company then won a major NASA cargo contract. SpaceX's later reusable rockets, crew flights and Starlink network made it a central launch and communications supplier to the federal government [[spacex-s1-2026, spacex-mission, time-fortune-2021]].

Musk joined Tesla in 2004 by leading its first institutional financing round and became chief executive in October 2008. He described the strategy in a 2006 post: begin with an expensive sports car, use the proceeds to build progressively cheaper cars and add zero-emission energy products. Tesla went public in 2010, expanded through the Model S and Model 3, and made most of Musk's publicly visible wealth before the SpaceX offering [[tesla-bio, tesla-master-plan-2006, tesla-master-plan-2016]].

The combination also tied his private interests to public policy. Tesla benefited from energy and vehicle policy, while SpaceX earned federal launch, satellite and defense business. Those relationships do not make company contracts personal political contributions, but they became central to conflict-of-interest questions once Musk entered the White House [[spacex-s1-2026, gao-doge-personnel-2026]].

chapters.title: Regulation, Twitter and control of a platform
chapters.dek: A securities-law settlement preceded the $44 billion purchase that turned an executive into a platform owner.
chapters.body:
Musk's use of social media had already produced a governance dispute before he owned a platform. In August 2018 he posted that he had secured funding to take Tesla private at $420 a share. The SEC alleged that the claim lacked an adequate basis; Musk and Tesla settled without admitting or denying the allegations. Musk stepped down as Tesla chair for three years, both paid penalties and Tesla agreed to oversee specified communications [[sec-tesla-settlement-2018]].

In April 2022 Musk offered to buy Twitter after accumulating a large stake. He completed the $44 billion transaction on October 27 after attempting to terminate the merger agreement and being sued by Twitter. The company became privately controlled by Musk and was later renamed X [[twitter-13d-2022, sec-twitter-complaint-2026]].

Musk said the acquisition was about speech and public trust. Ownership also gave him power over distribution, moderation and the platform on which he made endorsements, interviewed Trump and promoted America PAC. In 2025 xAI acquired X, and in February 2026 SpaceX acquired the xAI parent, placing the platform, the Grok model and AI infrastructure within the publicly traded SpaceX group [[ted-2022, spacex-10q-2026, tesla-proxy-2026]].

chapters.title: The largest donor of the 2024 election
chapters.dek: An endorsement after the Butler shooting became a turnout organization and at least $277 million in spending.
chapters.body:
Musk had previously donated to candidates in both parties and described himself as politically mixed. In 2022 he said he had voted Republican for the first time. His decisive move came on July 13, 2024, when he endorsed Donald Trump minutes after the attempted assassination in Butler, Pennsylvania [[x-endorsement-2024, cnn-immigration-2024]].

Musk created and financed America PAC, which paid for canvassing, digital advertising and other turnout work in battleground states. On October 5 he appeared with Trump at the Butler site, called himself 'Dark MAGA' and warned that the election could be the last if Trump lost [[ap-butler-2024]].

Filings available in December put Musk's spending for Trump and other Republicans at no less than $277 million, the most of any individual donor that cycle. CBS reported $239 million to America PAC and also linked Musk to RBG PAC, which used Ruth Bader Ginsburg's name in ads arguing that her abortion position resembled Trump's; Ginsburg's granddaughter called that use an affront to her legacy [[cbs-donations-2024, fec-musk]].

chapters.title: Four months inside the White House
chapters.dek: A temporary advisory role drove personnel and contract cuts, while later audits questioned the savings ledger.
chapters.body:
Trump's January 20, 2025 executive order renamed the U.S. Digital Service as the U.S. DOGE Service and created a temporary organization to pursue an eighteen-month efficiency agenda. Musk was not the USDS administrator. GAO later established that he worked in the White House as a special government employee and senior adviser, advised USDS personnel and was publicly described by Trump as leading the overall DOGE effort [[white-house-doge-order-2025, gao-doge-personnel-2026]].

The effort pressed agencies to reduce staff, terminate grants and contracts, sell property and change information systems. Musk initially discussed savings on a far larger scale than DOGE later claimed. His temporary service ended May 30, when Trump staged a departure event in the Oval Office [[ap-doge-departure-2025, white-house-departure-2025]].

Later review separated the existence of cuts from their claimed value. In August 2026 GAO reported that DOGE's Wall of Receipts listed $110 billion in savings from contracts, grants and leases through July 7, but found incorrect estimates, unsupported calculations and 108 leases already being phased out before DOGE. GAO recommended prominent disclosure of the data's limits. The findings do not erase every termination; they mean the displayed total was not a verified measure of net federal savings [[gao-doge-receipts-2026]].

Musk's company holdings created recurring ethics questions because several agencies affected by federal policy also regulated or contracted with his businesses. GAO documented that ethics officials advised on recusals and financial conflicts; its report did not conclude that every DOGE action involving those agencies was directed by Musk or violated the law [[gao-doge-personnel-2026]].

chapters.title: Break with Trump and return to Republican finance
chapters.dek: The threatened third party did not replace America PAC or Republican super PACs.
chapters.body:
Within a week of leaving government, Musk attacked Trump's tax and spending bill as inconsistent with DOGE's deficit-cutting mission. The dispute escalated on June 5: Trump threatened federal support for Musk's companies, and Musk endorsed impeachment and made an allegation involving unreleased Epstein records that he later deleted. Musk subsequently said some of his posts had gone too far [[reuters-feud-2025]].

On July 5 Musk announced that an 'America Party' had been formed. He said it would challenge the two-party system and oppose lawmakers who backed the spending law, but the announcement did not become the main vehicle for his next election campaign [[reuters-america-party-2025]].

By the 2026 midterms Musk was again the largest known individual donor, now to Republican organizations. Associated Press reported more than $276 million since July, including $158 million to Senate Leadership Fund and $76 million to America PAC. The PAC revived the turnout operation it had used in 2024 and spent in competitive congressional races [[ap-midterms-2026, reuters-midterms-2026, fec-musk]].

chapters.title: SpaceX goes public and the companies converge
chapters.dek: A record offering brought rockets, satellites, X and xAI under one public-company roof.
chapters.body:
SpaceX acquired the parent of xAI and X on February 2, 2026. Its filings described three businesses: launch and spacecraft, Starlink connectivity, and an AI segment spanning Grok, X and computing infrastructure. Tesla separately invested $2 billion in SpaceX after its planned xAI investment converted in the merger [[spacex-10q-2026, tesla-proxy-2026]].

On June 15 SpaceX completed an initial public offering of about 638.9 million shares at $135 each, producing roughly $85.7 billion in net proceeds. The filing preserved Musk's control through the company's voting structure while making the value of his holdings visible to public markets [[spacex-ipo-8k, spacex-s1-2026]].

Forbes estimated Musk's wealth at $989 billion after market close on October 21. The exact number changes with public share prices and estimates of less liquid holdings, but the source of political capacity is clear: concentrated ownership in companies whose market values, federal business and communications reach all expanded during the period in which his election spending reached record levels [[forbes-net-worth-2026, tesla-13g-2026, spacex-10q-2026]].
